headline: Dry, foggy Thursday and Friday; wetter, windier weather arrives Tuesday.
summary: A weakening swirl of low pressure aloft is drifting south off the Oregon coast, while a weak front fades over the southern part of the region. Next, a ridge of high pressure aloft slides over western Washington, bringing a mostly dry, gray stretch Thursday and Friday, with highs near 50 and foggy mornings, especially inland and in river valleys. Friday should turn sunny. Another upper-level low forms off Oregon over the weekend, and forecasters are unsure where it will settle, which decides whether showers reach western Washington or only graze it. A more organized front arrives Tuesday, bringing the first clearly wetter, windier weather and rising snow levels in the mountains, meaning the elevation where snow falls moves up. Confidence is high for Thursday, Friday, and Tuesday; lower for the weekend.
